evals.prompt: I want to build a habit tracker app. Thinking streaks, a social feed, an AI coach, gamification, an Apple Watch app, leaderboards, and maybe a Notion integration. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to start building all of it. Forces a single essential intent (the one thing the habit tracker must do), scores the proposed features against it with the 90% rule, keeps only 9-10s, parks the rest. Produces ESSENTIAL_INTENT.md with intent, vital few, non-goals, parked list.
expectations: No feature is built before one essential intent with a done-when is stated
Each of the seven proposed features is scored with the 90% rule and only 9s and 10s are kept
Parked features are listed as parked, not deleted
An ESSENTIAL_INTENT.md file is written with the intent, the done-when and the parked list

evals.prompt: The todo CLI works great. While we're at it let's also add tags, due dates, recurring tasks, a web UI, and cloud sync. Sound good?
evals.expected_output: Detects the scope creep trip wires ('while we're at it', 'also add'). Re-anchors to the essential intent. Scores each new feature, pushes back on the non-essential ones, parks them rather than agreeing to all. Does not just say 'sounds good' and pile them on.
expectations: The scope-creep phrases ('while we're at it', 'also add') are named as the trigger
The reply re-states the existing essential intent before scoring the five additions
At least one of the five additions is pushed back on and parked
The reply does not agree to all five additions

evals.prompt: Help me make a SaaS for freelancers.
evals.expected_output: Does not immediately sprawl into a big feature list / tech stack. Forces clarity on the single essential outcome and who it's for before any building. Asks the essential-intent questions, narrows to one sharp sentence.
expectations: No feature list or tech stack is proposed before the essential outcome is clear
The reply asks who the single user is and what one problem the SaaS solves
The intent is narrowed to one sentence with a done-when before anything is built

evals.prompt: ok so i have this idea, kind of a marketplace but also a community, for like home cooks? or maybe meal preppers. people could sell food, or share recipes, maybe do subscriptions, and i want reviews and a map and messaging and maybe AI meal plans. idk where to even start, my brain is everywhere on this.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a disorganized tangle. Does NOT start building or list features. Grills with a few sharp, convergence-forcing questions (one person/one problem, done-when, two-week ultimatum), pushes back on mush, narrows to one essential intent with a done-when, defines a smallest shippable slice and a single next action, names the biggest obstacle, parks the rest.
expectations: The reply asks at most a few convergence-forcing questions (one person, one problem, done-when, two-week ultimatum)
No feature list and no code is produced before the essential intent is fixed
Vague answers are pushed back on rather than accepted
The result is one essential intent with a done-when, the rest parked

evals.prompt: ok so i'm a solo founder and i want to build a 'all-in-one workspace for freelancers': invoicing, time tracking, contracts, a client portal, proposals, expense scanning, calendar sync, a mobile app, ai email drafts, a marketplace for leads, tax estimates, and team chat. i have maybe 10 hrs a week and a laptop. where do i even start
evals.expected_output: The agent grills the founder with a few sharp questions, locks one essential intent with a done-when, scores the twelve features with the 90% rule and parks the non-essential ones, then defines one smallest slice and one next action.
expectations: The agent asks at most three focused clarifying questions about one user, one problem, and an observable outcome before proposing a build plan
A single essential intent sentence is stated and it contains an explicit done-when condition
Features from the list are each given a 0-10 score and anything below 9 is placed in a Parked list rather than deleted
An ESSENTIAL_INTENT.md file is written with sections for smallest shippable slice, next action, vital few, non-goals and parked
The output ends with exactly one concrete next action, not a menu of options

evals.prompt: The todo CLI in ~/src/tdo works great now. While we're at it let's also add tags, due dates, recurring tasks, a web UI and cloud sync. I'd like to get all of it into the 1.0 release on Dec 15.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the scope-creep trip wires, restates the existing intent, scores tags, due dates, recurring tasks, web UI and cloud sync against it, and parks the sub-9 items instead of agreeing to all of them.
expectations: The agent explicitly flags that the request adds scope beyond the working CLI and re-anchors to an intent statement
Each of the five proposed features receives a 0-10 score with a one-line reason
Features scoring below 9 are parked with their score, not silently dropped and not built
The agent does not simply agree to add all five features to the 1.0 release
The response names a single smallest slice or next action for the release

evals.prompt: i have 5 side projects going (a chrome extension, a podcast, a newsletter, a rust game engine, and an etsy shop) plus a full-time job and i'm honestly overwhelmed. nothing is getting finished. help me figure out what to do
evals.expected_output: The agent applies the loop to commitments: asks what the one outcome matters most, ranks the five projects against it, picks one priority to advance this week, and parks or declines the rest with a captured list.
expectations: The agent asks a sharp clarifying question to force a decision (for example which one project matters most or what finished looks like) instead of listing generic productivity tips
All five side projects are scored or ranked against one stated outcome, with only a clear 9-10 kept active
The non-selected projects are recorded in a parked list, not discarded
Exactly one project and one concrete next action for this week are named
The agent identifies one obstacle to remove first or adds a time buffer to the plan
